source: Sampled from real pixels of the YellowSense poster (1.webp, 970x2000); median of matching pixels in the named region.

black_headline.note: effectively pure black; headings inside feature blocks measure #0F0F0E

orange_headline.note: an amber/ochre orange, darker and browner than a typical safety orange

deep_orange_logo.where: ring mark and YELLOWSENSE wordmark (wordmark measures #C36D0F)
deep_orange_logo.note: use #C26E10 as the single logo orange

mustard_banner.note: deep mustard/amber; same hue family as the headline orange, slightly darker

cream_background.where: poster page background (top, left strip, feature card, QR card)
cream_background.note: Measured background is a warm near-white, not a visible cream. For a true cream feel use the suggested #FBF7F0.

accent_red_orange.where: feature-card headings (SECURE AUTHENTICATION etc.), EXPLORE MORE (#C15525), AI Era (#CA5E1D)

banner_text_white.where: VISION / MISSION / IMPACT text and icons on the banner

glow_orange.where: fingertip scan glow in hero photo

phone_ui_yellow.where: progress bar on the phone-screen UI

logo_yellowsense.png.use_on: light backgrounds only (the grey sub-line disappears on dark)

contrast_notes.guidance: brandOrange and headlineOrange are about 3.6:1 on cream: fine for large display type (headlines, big numbers) only. Use orangeTextSmall or accent for body-size orange text. White on the banner is 4.05:1: bold or large text only.
logo_yellowsense_onDark.png orange (#F79320) matches brandOrange here. Do not place logo_yellowsense.png (grey sub-line) on dark.

suggested.derived_note: bg #FBF7F0, surfaces, muted inks, rules and all dark-theme values are DERIVED suggestions, not sampled. Everything under 'measured' is sampled.
